content.text: The text combines horticultural commentary, literary bibliography, and a serialized story about the Shaw family. The gardening discussion celebrates French and English gardens, landscape design, flowers, orchards, planting, horticultural writers, and famous garden lovers. The bibliography catalogs German and French translations and criticism of Laurence Sterne, followed by an index and listed textual errors. The narrative centers on Pauline, Hilary, and Patience Shaw in Winton. Pauline writes Uncle Paul, who funds their summer diversions. Hilary moves to The Maples farm, later returns to the remodeled spare room, and receives a horse, trap, camera, and boat. The sisters create the “Seeing Winton First Club,” exploring the village, church, manor, lake, schoolhouse, gardens, and countryside. Their activities include picnics, drives, photography, boating, and welcoming Sextoness Jane. Uncle Paul visits the parsonage, reconciles with his brother, and offers Pauline and Hilary schooling away from home.
